Skip entry animation when restoring pending snackbar

Before:
https://screencast.googleplex.com/cast/NjAyNjE2MzczNzU5MTgwOHxmYThiYWZmZC03Ng

After:
https://screencast.googleplex.com/cast/NTYxNzc1MzM4NDgxMjU0NHxhZDliYmMyNC0zMg

When applying or undoing an NTP theme (or when a background download
completes), Activity#recreate() destroys and recreates the activity
while the Apply, Undo, or Redo snackbar is on screen. Currently, the
restored snackbar in the recreated activity plays the slide-in
animation a second time, causing a double-bounce effect.

Add Snackbar#setAnimateIn(boolean) and skip the translation-Y entry
animation in SnackbarView#show() when shouldAnimateIn() is false.
CrossDeviceSettingImporter sets animateIn to false when restoring a
pending snackbar across activity recreation in
maybeShowPendingSnackbar().

Bug: 517615321, 458057621

[crypto] Drop extra thread hop in MaybeMeasureTpmOperations

MaybeMeasureTpmOperations() posted its own thread pool task, but its
only caller (ChromeBrowserMainExtraPartsMetrics::PostBrowserStart())
already calls it from a delayed, CONTINUE_ON_SHUTDOWN thread pool task.
Run the measurement on the calling sequence instead, which removes a
needless thread hop.

Ash: Migrate FloatingWorkspaceService off ProfileHelper

This changelist is part of an ongoing series to decouple ChromeOS
code from the main Chrome browser codebase. By migrating away from
ash::ProfileHelper (//chrome/browser/ash) to lower-level Ash APIs such
as ash::BrowserContextHelper (//chromeos/ash/components), it removes
inappropriate upward dependencies from lower-level Ash components to
the higher-level browser application layer. This modernization also
moves code away from heavy, UI-bound Profile objects and toward the
cleaner content::BrowserContext abstraction. Where ProfileHelper wraps
user checks, the migration uses components/user_manager directly.

FloatingWorkspaceService now resolves active-user profiles through
BrowserContextHelper. This keeps desk uploads and user-switch handling
on the lower-level browser-context boundary while preserving the
existing profile identity checks.

Ash: Migrate website reporting tests off ProfileHelper

This changelist is part of an ongoing series to decouple ChromeOS
code from the main Chrome browser codebase. By migrating away from
ash::ProfileHelper (//chrome/browser/ash) to lower-level Ash APIs such
as ash::BrowserContextHelper (//chromeos/ash/components), it removes
inappropriate upward dependencies from lower-level Ash components to
the higher-level browser application layer. This modernization also
moves code away from heavy, UI-bound Profile objects and toward the
cleaner content::BrowserContext abstraction. Where ProfileHelper wraps
user checks, the migration uses components/user_manager directly.

WebsiteEventsObserverBrowserTest and
WebsiteUsageTelemetrySamplerBrowserTest now resolve their affiliated
account through BrowserContextHelper and convert the result at the
existing Profile boundary. Both fixtures log in the real affiliated
user before calling profile(), so they no longer need ProfileHelper's
testing-map wrapper or its local build and DEPS permissions.

Ash: Migrate file system provider paths off ProfileHelper

This changelist is part of an ongoing series to decouple ChromeOS
code from the main Chrome browser codebase. By migrating away from
ash::ProfileHelper (//chrome/browser/ash) to lower-level Ash APIs such
as ash::BrowserContextHelper (//chromeos/ash/components), it removes
inappropriate upward dependencies from lower-level Ash components to
the higher-level browser application layer. This modernization also
moves code away from heavy, UI-bound Profile objects and toward the
cleaner content::BrowserContext abstraction. Where ProfileHelper wraps
user checks, the migration uses components/user_manager directly.

GetMountPath() now resolves user identity through the lower-level
browser-context boundary, and URL parsing uses the matching context
classification. The affected tests register the account and annotate its
browser context. This keeps the account relationship intact without
changing session state.

Ash: Migrate device trust signals test off ProfileHelper

This changelist is part of an ongoing series to decouple ChromeOS
code from the main Chrome browser codebase. By migrating away from
ash::ProfileHelper (//chrome/browser/ash) to lower-level Ash APIs such
as ash::BrowserContextHelper (//chromeos/ash/components), it removes
inappropriate upward dependencies from lower-level Ash components to
the higher-level browser application layer. This modernization also
moves code away from heavy, UI-bound Profile objects and toward the
cleaner content::BrowserContext abstraction. Where ProfileHelper wraps
user checks, the migration uses components/user_manager directly.

AshSignalsDecoratorBrowserTest now resolves its signed-in user and
login-screen context through the lower-level browser-context layer. The
browser fixture starts with an associated stub-user context, and browser
startup loads the sign-in context before the tests run, so neither path
needs ProfileHelper's compatibility or creation behavior.

omnibox: Re-enable the popup's in-process theme colors test

OmniboxPopupUITest.PopulateLocalResourceLoaderConfig expected a
ThemeColorsSourceManager, but ThemeColorsSourceManagerFactory returns
none when kWebUIInProcessResourceLoadingV2 is disabled. The
*-no-initial-webui-rel builders disable that feature on the command
line, so the test failed there and was disabled.

The test now runs in a fixture that sets the feature explicitly, and is
parameterized over its state. With the feature off it checks that the
popup leaves chrome://theme/colors.css to the network, which the old
test did not cover.

[Journeys] Resolve journey collections

The journey details page shows collections as sections, so resolved
journeys need them in the same form as their visits. Resolve collection
items against the journey's resolved visits. As collections are
optional, items that don't match one of the journey's visits are
dropped, as are collections left empty; neither drops the journey.

Surfacing collections in the Topics UI will follow separately.

[Journeys] Sync journey collections

Journeys can group similar pages into titled collections, which are now
stored in the history database (crrev.com/c/8529735). Fill them in from
sync so that they reach local storage, and drop them from the cached
remote specifics now that they are stored locally.

Journeys synced before this change only get collections once the server
changes them again. This is fine, since the feature is not launched yet.

NO_IFTTT=Proto fields were added in crrev.com/c/8524751

[Journeys] Share gtest printers for journey types

The resolved journey types are about to get gtest printers too. Move the
printers for the stored types out of journeys_database_unittest.cc into
a shared test-only file, so that all journey printers live in one place
and every test that prints these types uses the same printer.

967c1cbec0c212dee6dd3cab7edf55e82731ee13 [ diff ] 
printing: Bind target frame ID at initiatePrint on Android

Android's 3-stage print lifecycle previously used -1/-1 sentinel frame
coordinates when initiated from the browser menu, re-resolving the
target frame on each JNI hop. If the initiating frame navigated or
entered BackForwardCache before dialog dismissal, finishPrint() targeted
the new primary main frame instead of the frame that entered printing
mode, leaving the cached frame stuck in printing state.

Bind the print session to the target frame's GlobalRenderFrameHostId at
session initiation and propagate that identity across subsequent print()
and finishPrint() calls. Decouple FinishPrint() lookup from active-frame
selection so teardown always reaches the originating frame as long as it
remains live.

TAG=agy
CONV=481a86f4-576b-401a-b6ab-ac7b7a0fd3e1

[CRD host] Validate calling extension origin in remote_webauthn

remote_webauthn only verified that it was launched by Google Chrome.
A user-level native messaging host manifest could point to the
genuine remote_webauthn binary and list an arbitrary extension in
allowed_origins, letting that extension drive the WebAuthn proxy.

Chrome always passes the calling extension origin as the first
positional argument to native messaging hosts, so remote_webauthn now
rejects callers whose origin is not one of the CRD WebAuthn
extensions. The extension ID list is moved from
RemoteWebAuthnExtensionNotifier to remote_webauthn_constants so that
it can be shared by both.

Note that, consistent with the generated NMH manifest, release builds
only accept the prod extensions, so a local release build of
remote_webauthn will reject the dev extensions even though
register_local_nm_hosts.sh registers them.

button, so the button fires one event with the original keyboard or
mouse event; hosts can drop the cancel icon (X), and no host uses
32px height.

bluetooth: Stop discovery when advertisement clients are cleared

ClearAdvertisementClients() dropped the scanning and watch
advertisements clients on tab hide or focus loss without releasing the
underlying discovery sessions, so the platform (BlueZ) scan stayed
active for the lifetime of the tab; call MaybeStopDiscovery() so the
session is released together with its last client.

ServiceWorker: Flush decoder when loading installed scripts

ServiceWorkerInstalledScriptsManager::GetScriptData() decodes the
installed script body using TextResourceDecoder::Decode(), but omitted
calling decoder->Flush().

Because TextResourceDecoder buffers up to 3 bytes for BOM detection
and TextCodec buffers incomplete multi-byte sequences, omitting Flush()
causes scripts smaller than 3 bytes to decode into empty strings, and
incomplete multi-byte sequences at EOF to drop their trailing
replacement characters (U+FFFD).

This diverged from WorkerClassicScriptLoader::DidFinishLoading(), which
always flushes the decoder upon completing the initial network load.
This CL calls decoder->Flush() at the end of GetScriptData() and appends
any remaining flushed text, ensuring consistent decoded source text
between network and installed script loads.

Increase browser_tests shards on win-asan from 120 to 140

Even after disabling WebUIOmniboxPopup (https://crrev.com/c/8535352) and
default renderer prewarming in InProcessBrowserTest
(https://crrev.com/c/8542233) on win-asan, browser_tests shard durations
remain close enough to the 60m timeout limit that slower shards still
time out.

Increase the number of shards from 120 to 140 to provide additional
runtime headroom and prevent shard timeouts.

[ChoMenu GlowUp] Keep mnemonics in row style menu items and their submenus

This CL uses the hooks added in the parent CL 8531890. BrowserActions
sets actions::kMnemonicTextKey on the row menu items. The value is the
same string (only the '...' were removed using
chrome::GetMnemonicTitleText()). GetText() was not changed, so toolbar
buttons, tooltips and search are not affected.

Also, for rows that have text override, ActionAppMenu applies it with
MenuItemView::SetTitleOverride(). This way whenever an action is updated
its row menu item keeps its mnemonic.

ServiceWorker: Respect encoding for top-level worker scripts

Plumb the resolved TextEncoding of top-level classic worker scripts from
WorkerClassicScriptLoader and InstalledScriptsManager::ScriptData
through to ServiceWorkerScriptCachedMetadataHandler::Encoding().

This ensures that the script encoding is taken into account when
generating and matching V8 code cache for service worker scripts.
Guarded by the new runtime-enabled feature.

See the bug for details.

[NTP Aurora V2] Align beside-MVT AI Mode card with MVT tiles and hide tile icon backgrounds

This CL updates the styling and alignment of the AI Mode card and Most
Visited Tiles when the beside-MVT layout (NTP Aurora V2) is enabled:

- Vertical Alignment: Aligns the top and bottom paddings of the
  beside-MVT AI Mode card with the MVT container so the AI Mode icon
  and label line up with the MVT tiles across both default and Aurora
  V1 padding styles.

- Two-Line Title Wrapping: Allows the beside-MVT AI Mode button label
  to wrap up to 2 lines with centered horizontal gravity when large
  font sizes are used, matching the "Add new" MVT button behavior, and
  keeps both cards at matching heights.

- Remove Circular Tile Backgrounds when the beside-MVT module is
  enabled.

Screenshots: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1bMRVyyqOd0-cAmyTbL9IhKNU9uSvDdpdCngSzSXIHnk/edit?tab=t.0#bookmark=id.7r569vl0hwq7

LHS: Update --ntp-search-box-width's break points to base on RHS width

Before, the break points relied on @media min-width, which refers to the
window width. With LHS taking up space (follow-up CL), these numbers
will no longer be accurate. This change updated the break point rules to
reference the RHS width instead.

Remove exit time destructor in WaylandDataDeviceBase

Change the return type of WaylandDataDeviceBase::GetAvailableMimeTypes()
to a span, instead of exposing the underlying container type by
const-ref. Then if the underlying container is not available,
GetAvailableMimeTypes() can just return an empty span, instead of being
forced to instantiate an empty vector which comes with an exit time
destructor. Then change the GetAvailableMimeTypes() to copy the return
value appropriately.

LHS: Move voice search dialog into #rhsContent

In order to accommodate LHS, we put the existing #content of NTP into a
RHS div in crrev.com/c/8542238. In the next crrev.com/c/8544436, we'll
update the @media (min-width) queries in NTP app.css to @container
rhsContent (mid-width) instead, where we overwrite css variables that
the voice search dialog depends on. But because #voiceSearchDialog sits
outside of #rhsContent right now, it won't inherit the overwrites.

As a fix, this change moves #voiceSearchDialog into #rhsContent.

This change should have no behavior change:
- The dialog is opened with showModal(), so it renders in the top layer and its DOM position doesn't affect stacking or layout.
- It's added to COMPOSEBOX_INERT_ALLOWLIST so that it isn't made inert along with the other direct children of #rhsContent while the composebox is open.

Decisions API: Route AIManager to the language model (Gemma 4) backend

Lets AIManager create AILanguageModelDecisionModel (crrev.com/c/8500743),
the only Decisions API backend for now.

- Uses the Prompt API's foundation model and use case resolution
  (PromptApiFeatureConfig via the manifest broker), reusing the existing
  Gemma 4 delivery.
- Requires OnDeviceModelForceCpuBackend as a temporary workaround for
  GPU backend scoring issues (crbug.com/571218294); otherwise
  CanCreateDecisionModel() reports kUnavailableFeatureNotEnabled.
- chrome://flags#decisions-api also enables the manifest broker, Gemma 4
  and OnDeviceModelForceCpuBackend, which affect all built-in AI APIs.

Decisions API: Add language model (Gemma 4) backend

Adds AILanguageModelDecisionModel, a blink.mojom.AIDecisionModel that
scores options using the Prompt API's on-device foundation model
(e.g. Gemma 4) and the shared schema compiler (crrev.com/c/8519223).
Not wired up to AIManager yet.

- DecisionModelPromptBuilder builds the system, input, and per-question
  prompts, mapping each option to a distinct letter key (A, B, ...) for
  single-token Session::Score() evaluation.
- create() checks that the system prompt plus each question fit within
  the token quota (failing with kInitialInputTooLarge otherwise).
- decide() checks that the input fits (kErrorInputTooLarge), appends the
  system prompt and input once to a fresh session, and scores each
  question and option on cloned session states before normalizing via
  DecodeResult().
- Serializes decide() calls in order at the page's current priority, and
  uses the Prompt API's ModelClient, token limit, and health reporting.

Set `text-size-adjust: calc(100% * env(preferred-text-scale))` on `body`

Customize Chrome: Make side panel resize horizontally

On Android the side panel WebContents can be 400px (wide), 348px
(narrow), or as little as 200px wide (shrink-to-fit). On desktop the
panel defaults to 360px but can be dragged wider.

Make the Customize Chrome side panel adapt to these widths:
* Scale the inline padding (--sp-card-inline-padding) linearly from
  16px at >=360px down to 8px at 200px, and derive the grid gap from it
  (8px -> 4px). All hardcoded 16/32/48px inline paddings and margins now
  reference these variables, so desktop at >=360px is unchanged.
* Keep color tiles square and scale them with the grid; make the color
  circle padding a percentage so the circle scales with its tile.
* Hide the segmented button icons via a container query when there is
  not enough room for icon + label.
* Cap content at 400px (Android's widest) and keep it start-aligned when
  the desktop panel is dragged wider than that.

See go/customize-chrome-resizing-validation for some screenshots
(googler only)

[crubit] Enable `assume_lifetimes` by default in `rust_api_from_cpp`.

Without lifetime annotations, Crubit binds C++ references (including
`this`) as raw pointers, which makes most methods `unsafe` to call from
Rust.  Crubit's `assume_lifetimes` feature applies Rust's lifetime
elision rules instead (e.g. `this` becomes `&self`).

This CL:

* Adds `assume_lifetimes` to the Crubit features enabled for all
  `rust_api_from_cpp` targets.
* Adds `//build/rust/crubit:cref` for Rust code that uses `CRef` or
  `CMut` (the types of C++ references returned from the bindings).
* Adds a short "References and lifetimes" section to
  `docs/rust/crubit/rust_api_from_cpp.md`.  The section links to
  Crubit's docs and covers Chromium-specific details.
* Adds tests for elided and for explicit lifetimes.

info, and logged
Autofill.PaymentsChurnedUsersUi.ShowResult.NoAccountInfoPresent if
empty. Because this logic is platform-agnostic, running it in the UI
delegate meant it only executed on Desktop and was bypassed on Clank
(Android).

This CL centralizes the account info retrieval and metric logging in
PaymentsChurnedUsersManager::OnFieldTypesDetermined:
- If extended AccountInfo is empty, logs kNoAccountInfoPresent and exits early.
- Otherwise, passes the retrieved AccountInfo to
PaymentsChurnedUsersUiDelegate::ShowPaymentsChurnedUsersUI(AccountInfo,
...).
- Updates PaymentsChurnedUsersUiDelegate implementations on Desktop and Android to accept AccountInfo.
- Updates unit tests and browser tests accordingly.

Testing screenshot:
- https://screenshot-v2.corp.google.com/63jYXZAPdwrgmV3
- See histogram shows #7 kNoAccountInfoPresent
(https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:components/autofill/core/browser/payments/payments_churned_users_metrics.h;l=27)
with dash, meaning that kNoAccountInfoPresent is triggered
- The bottomsheet also doesn't appear in the testing webpage and #0 kShown
(https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:components/autofill/core/browser/payments/payments_churned_users_metrics.h;l=20)
is not triggered.

Ensure GatherObservations references remain safe to use

In ResizeObserver::GatherObservations(), ObservationSizeOutOfSync() and
TargetDepth() can trigger a synchronous update which adds to
`observations_` and reallocates its backing buffer. Using `auto&` bound
a `const WeakMember<ResizeObservation>&` directly into that buffer,
which was unsafe to use if the buffer moved. Using `ResizeObservation*`
instead copies the pointer and is valid even if `observations_`
reallocates.

[crd host][mac] Check caller UID when brokering host services

AgentProcessBroker runs as root and forwards ChromotingHostServices
receivers to the active agent process. It only validated the caller's
code signature, so a signed helper running as one user could bind the
session services of another user's active agent.

Record each agent's real UID when it registers, and reject
BindChromotingHostServices() when the caller's real UID does not match
the active agent's UID. This matches the per-user isolation that Linux
(require_same_peer_user) and Windows (session ID check) already have.

Replace IsRootProcessGetter with ProcessUidGetter so tests can fake
both root-ness and per-user identity through the same seam.

[SideUi] Compare SideUiShowability IDs as sets (3/5)

Make SideUiShowability hold sets of IDs instead of lists.
-Previously, SideUiShowability#equals compared lists, so the order the
 IDs were added in mattered. Since paused containers are now laid out
 first, pausing or resuming a container could reorder the IDs and
 notify SideUiObservers of a showability change when nothing changed.
-The previous CL worked around this by sorting the IDs.
-Now, the IDs are sets, so their order doesn't matter, and the sort is
 removed. Consumers only check whether an ID is (un)showable.

parent
78005cd1d1f9e3f97b906be2e95d493ad41a4560 [ diff ] 
[SideUi] Add API to pause Side UI updates (2/5)

Add SideUiCoordinator#pauseSideUiUpdates and #resumeSideUiUpdates.
-Previously, any Side UI update could resize, re-position or detach a
 container at any time. This breaks e.g. a tab drag that started from
 the vertical tabs rail if the rail changes mid-drag.
-Now, a paused container keeps the size it had when it was paused,
 and keeps reserving that width, so the web contents and the other
 containers lay out around it. Other containers are laid out as if it
 had the highest priority, so they may be auto-closed to make room for
 it. It isn't asked for its showable size or whether it has content to
 show while paused.
-A paused container gets no update or auto-close/restore callbacks.
 Resuming runs one non-animated update (UpdateReason#UPDATES_RESUMED)
 that applies the latest state, and may auto-close or auto-restore the
 resumed container.
-Pausing ends any in-progress animation first. It isn't ref-counted,
 and unregistering a paused container resumes it first.

[Omnibox] Truncate Fusebox popup row text after 2 lines

Per the Plus Menu Design Iteration UX spec, Fusebox (+) popup row
labels should wrap to at most 2 lines and end with an ellipsis instead
of growing without limit at large font sizes or with long
translations.

* Sets maxLines=2 and ellipsize=end on @id/action_text in
  fusebox_list_item.xml. This covers both static rows inflated from
  XML and dynamically bound rows; recent-tab rows keep their existing
  1-line override in FuseboxViewBinder.
* Removes android:singleLine from Fusebox.PopupMenu.Item. The style is
  applied to the row's LinearLayout root, which ignores TextView
  attributes, so it was a misleading no-op.
* Adds FuseboxViewBinderUnitTest#listItems_truncateAfterTwoLines.

[Glic] Fix stale recreation state override clobbering expanded Show

When an Actor task tab is detached into BackgroundTabPool (e.g. when
Chrome is backgrounded), GlicSidePanelCoordinatorAndroid::OnTabWillDetach
and OnTabWillDeactivate call SaveStateBeforeDeactivation(), which saves
initial_state_override_for_activity_recreation_ = kPeeked if the Glic
bottom sheet was in peek mode.

When the user subsequently taps an Actor notification and the live
background tab is restored into the TabModel before
TabBottomSheetManagerImpl finishes initializing on the window
(!tab_bottom_sheet_bridge_->IsManagerReady()):
1. OnTabDidActivate calls Show(kPeeked), deferring to
   pending_show_options_.
2. GlicKeyedService.maybeInvokeGlic calls Show(kExpanded), updating
   pending_show_options_->initial_state to kExpanded.
3. When OnManagerInitialized fires, it unconditionally overwrites
   pending_show_options_->initial_state (kExpanded) with the stale
   initial_state_override_for_activity_recreation_ (kPeeked). Opening
   the sheet in kPeeked immediately transitions the coordinator to
   State::kPeek, which causes GlicSidePanelUi::SidePanelStateChanged to
   deactivate and close the active conversation embedder.

Fix this by:
- Clearing initial_state_override_for_activity_recreation_ when Show()
  is called with InitialState::kExpanded, and once Show() completes.
- Preserving InitialState::kExpanded in pending_show_options_ if a
  subsequent Show(kPeeked) is called while waiting for manager
  initialization.

parent
fd24ed6bda13731e6256e2128637f8959d8593f4 [ diff ] 
Match cross-device themes by OsType, FormFactor, and DataType

Theme sync services on Desktop, iOS, and Android upload a single theme
entity per platform using fixed client tags ("current_theme",
"current_theme_ios", "android_theme_tag") rather than per-device GUID
client tags. As a result, CrossDeviceThemeTracker::ResolveDeviceInfo
previously failed to match any DeviceInfo when hashing device->guid(),
leaving theme_info.guid empty and causing GetThemeForDeviceGuid to
return nullptr for non-empty device GUIDs.

Since themes are synced per platform rather than per device, replace
GetBestMatchDeviceGuid and GetThemeForDeviceGuid with
GetBestMatchDeviceOsTypeAndFormFactor and
GetThemeForOsTypeAndFormFactor, matching synced themes by platform
DataType via OsTypeToDataType(os_type, form_factor). Store
syncer::DataType directly in DeviceThemeInfo instead of DeviceInfo
fields, and remove unused DeviceInfoTracker observation,
ResolveDeviceInfo, and per-device fields (guid, device_name,
form_factor, os_type) from CrossDeviceThemeTracker and DeviceThemeInfo.

[ROSP] Add startup window retention metric

Records a boolean histogram tracking whether windows automatically
restored on cold startup remain open 30 seconds after creation or are
closed early.

* Schedules a 30-second retention timer when a pending startup window
  is restored to record true to the
  Android.MultiWindow.StartupRestorationWindowRetained boolean
  histogram.
* Notifies TabbedStartupWindowPolicyDelegate when a finishing tabbed
  activity is destroyed to cancel any pending retention timer and
  record false to the boolean histogram.

[glic] Start benchmark: remove harness artifacts from the cold number

The default HTTP/1 EmbeddedTestServer closes the connection after every
response, so each guest script fetch paid a TCP+TLS handshake;
production serves the client over one HTTP/2 connection. The test client
also imported WebClientMode as a value, pulling the 46 KB generated API
into a three-deep import waterfall that production never fetches. And a
fresh test browser paid network-service initialization on the first
open.

Serve the guest from an H2 server (new
GlicBrowserTestMixin::set_glic_https_test_server() hook; other fixtures
are unchanged), make the client's API imports type-only with
modulepreload for the remaining two files, and warm the network service
with one navigation to a separate origin before the timer. The guest
origin is left cold on purpose: Chrome does not preconnect for Glic, so
its DNS/TCP/TLS is real cold-open cost. Also wait for a ready spare
renderer before timing, log nav/resource timing per iteration, and have
run_glic_start_benchmark.py report cold and warm separately.

[glic] Respect initially_hidden for the no-webview guest contents

When kGlicContentsInitiallyHidden is enabled, the warming pool creates
GlicNoWebviewContentsManager with initially_hidden=true so the guest
warms in the background without being treated as visible. That flag was
being ignored in two places.

First, the guest lives in a PrivilegedWebContents, and
PrivilegedWebContents::Create() had no way to pass initially_hidden
through, so the guest WebContents was always created visible.

Second, ApplySizeToGuest() unconditionally marked the guest visible. It
runs on guest navigation, including while warming or attached but
hidden, so even a hidden guest got flipped to visible on its first load.

This CL adds an optional PwcCreateOptions argument (with
initially_hidden) to PrivilegedWebContents::Create() and has the manager
pass it through. ApplySizeToGuest() now only marks the guest visible
when Glic itself is visible.

The loading/error overlay is left as is: it is only created once Glic is
visible, so it never needs to start hidden.

Tests cover PWC creation visibility and the manager keeping the guest
hidden through a navigation until Glic is shown.

[webapps] Select best bitmap frame in WebApkSingleIconHasher

When WebApkSingleIconHasher decodes a non-PNG/JPEG icon (such as a
multi-frame .ico file) via WebContents::DownloadImage, Blink's
ImageDownloaderImpl reverses the decoded frames into smallest-first
order (e.g., [16x16, 32x32, 48x48, 256x256] for Slack's favicon.ico).

Previously, WebApkSingleIconHasher::OnImageDownloaded hardcoded
bitmaps[0], sending the 16x16 frame to the WebAPK minting server for
both the launcher icon and the splash screen.

Instead, pass ideal_icon_size to OnImageDownloaded and use
SelectFaviconFrameIndices(sizes, {ideal_icon_size}, ...) to select the
best matching frame.

[ChroMenu GlowUp] Let action menu items keep mnemonic text.

A MenuItemView bound to an ActionItem resets its title to
ActionItem::GetText() whenever the action changes. For menus built from
actions, this means:

- The items get no mnemonic. GetText() has no "&" marker, because
  other surfaces such as buttons and tooltips would draw it literally.
- A title set with SetTitle() is lost on the next action change, e.g.
  when the action is enabled or disabled.

This CL:
- Lets ActionItem text keep its mnemonic marker, like "&Find". Use
  "&&" for a literal "&". GetText() now returns the text without the
  marker, so buttons and tooltips are not affected.
- Adds ActionItem::GetTextWithMnemonic(), which returns the text as
  set. Action-bound menu items show it instead of GetText().
- Fixes MenuItemView::GetMnemonic() for "&&", which shows a literal
  "&". It returned the next character, like 't' for "AT&&T".

Nothing sets either hook yet, so there is no behavior change. CL 8536615
uses both (follow up CL).

DISABLE_SPELLCHECKER

[WebApps] Allow fallback to min-size and unsized favicons in InstallableIconFetcher

Currently, IsCandidateBigEnough() in InstallableIconFetcher only accepts
favicon candidates that explicitly meet ideal_size (or are SVGs/touch
icons) and rejects unsized kFavicon candidates and default /favicon.ico
entries. This prevents manifestless sites that only provide a
multi-resolution /favicon.ico (such as 48x48 .ico files) or icons sized
between min_size (48px) and ideal_size from using their favicon during
installation.

Update FetchFaviconFromCandidates() to use a two-pass selection:
1. Prefer candidates known to meet ideal_size (including SVGs,
   sizes="any", and touch icons).
2. If none match, fall back to candidates meeting min_size or unsized
   favicons (including default /favicon.ico), letting
   ManifestIconDownloader verify that the decoded bitmap meets min_size.

[CALI] View Tree: Show View Info on Hover

This CL adds View Info UI, which shows basic info of a View on hover.
Specifically, in the View Tree, when a View Row gets pointer hover, its
background gains a blue highlight, and the Info Bar shows the View's:
* Java Class.
* Dimensions in PX.
* Dimensions in DP.

To prepare for planned features (multi-select; same UI on Screenshot),
this CL implements hover UI in a structured fashion:
* Add `ViewEngaged` (owned by `MainModel`) as source of truth, storing
  nullable `hover` (upcoming: `sels` for selections).
* `TreeVis`'s hover handling:
  * Interface: `setHover()` to assign / sync hover value.
  * Interface: `withTransaction()` to wrap View Tree changes in order to
    transact (i.e., hide - update - show) visuals (i.e., hover).
  * Internal: `hoverIndex` to reduce churn and for transactions (e.g.,
    remember which rendered UI highlight to clear).
* Centralized event dispatching for hover: Currently hover is only
  triggered and shown on the View Tree. To prepare for Screenshot
  inclusion, this CL uses `MainController` (with injected callback) as
  an intermediary dispatcher; thus hover-related event handling is:

  [Event trigger]        --> [Dispatcher]   -->  [UI change]
  TreeController             MainController      TreeController
  (ScreenshotController)                         (ScreenshotController)

  * Inside `MainController`, also update model hover state and
    View Info.

Additional code improvements: Add CTOR JSDoc; use CSS `contain` to
prevent layout spillover; refactor `ViewNode` parsing; update UI / state
clearing.

Details:
* index.html: `#div-info-bar`: Add `.view-info` that shows details about
  a View, to be shown when its View Row is hovered by the pointer:
  * Add `.view-class` for the View's Java Class.
  * Add `.view-dims` for the View's dimensions, dynamically shown as

[SidePanel] Allow users to resize the side panel (1/3)

Implement the SideUiContainer manual resize contract for the side panel,
behind EnableAndroidSidePanelManualResizing.
-Previously, the side panel always used its automatic wide/narrow width
 and SideUiCoordinator showed no resize handle for it.
-Now, supportsManualResize() follows the flag, so SideUiResizeHandler
 shows the handle bar and the double arrow pointer icon. The handle
 matches the container's inner padding so it doesn't overlap the panel.
-A drag updates a transient width on every frame. Releasing it keeps
 the width, clamped between the minimum width and 500dp. A tap on the
 handle doesn't change the width.
-The picked width applies to all entries in the window until the window
 is destroyed. It isn't persisted, so each new session starts with the
 automatic width.
-A picked width overrides the automatic width. It is clamped to at least
 the minimum container width, and at most 500dp or the available width,
 whichever is smaller.
-Hiding the panel mid-drag drops the drag state, since the framework
 removes the handle without committing the drag.

[ImmersivePlayer] Postpone surface callbacks until dimensions are set

Previously, XrSurfaceEntityHolderImpl initialized surface dimensions to
1x1 and immediately fired surfaceCreated and surfaceChanged(1, 1) when a
callback was registered in addCallback(). When entering immersive video
playback while paused, CompositorViewImpl attached the surface with 1x1
bounds before the actual video dimensions were applied, causing the
initial frame to be rendered into a 1x1 buffer and stretched across the
entire player panel until playback resumed.

This change leaves mCurrentSurfaceDimensions unset until
setSurfacePixelDimensions(width, height) is called with valid dimensions
and defers surfaceCreated/surfaceChanged notifications until then. It
also applies pending video dimensions before immersive video options on
startup so custom mesh generators receive the actual surface dimensions.

Demo: https://screencast.googleplex.com/cast/NTc3NjA0Mjg5NDU1NzE4NHxiZjY3NzE2MS0xZQ
